title: BECE Business Studies: Office Practice - Business Studies - The Reception Office
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A place in an organization where visitors are first received and attended to before they are directed to other departments is called the
questions.explain: The **Reception Office** is the first point of call or contact in a business premises where visitors, clients, and inquiries are initially received and processed.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The clerical staff specifically employed to receive, welcome, and direct visitors to the appropriate persons in an organization is the
questions.explain: A **Receptionist** is the frontline employee whose primary duty is to welcome and direct guests, as well as handle preliminary inquiries.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Why is the receptionist considered a highly important staff member in an organization?
options: They sign all the cheques and financial documents.
They project the first image and reputation of the business to the public.
They formulate all core business policies.
They audit the daily financial records.
questions.explain: The receptionist is the business's "image maker." Their behaviour and appearance give visitors the first impression of the organization, making their role critical.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an essential personal quality required of a good receptionist?
questions.explain: A receptionist must possess a pleasant disposition. **Cheerfulness**, politeness, and a welcoming attitude are vital qualities for putting visitors at ease.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following are positive attributes expected of a receptionist EXCEPT
questions.explain: A receptionist should treat all visitors fairly and with respect. **Partiality** (favouritism or bias) is unprofessional and reflects poorly on the organization.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When a visitor approaches the reception desk, the best immediate action for the receptionist to take is to
options: ignore the visitor until they speak first
politely welcome the visitor and ask how to help
shout for the security guard to check them
questions.explain: The proper procedure for receiving a visitor is to offer a prompt, polite greeting, inquire about the purpose of their visit, and offer them a seat if necessary.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a visitor requests to see a manager who is currently in a crucial meeting, the appropriate way for the receptionist to handle the situation is to
options: tell the visitor to go away and come back the next day
allow the visitor to walk straight into the meeting room
interrupt the meeting immediately to inform the manager
politely explain the situation and ask the visitor to wait or drop a message
questions.explain: To maintain office decorum, the receptionist should not interrupt closed meetings unless it is an absolute emergency. Instead, they should **politely explain the delay and take a message**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following describes an appropriate dress code for a professional office receptionist?
options: Ripped jeans and a sleeveless t-shirt
A neat, smart corporate or formal outfit
Heavy party makeup with highly revealing clothes
questions.explain: Since receptionists are the image makers of the company, their dressing must project professionalism. **A neat, smart corporate or formal outfit** is required.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The document kept at the reception desk to record the names, addresses, and time of arrival of guests to the organization is the
questions.explain: A **visitor's book** is officially maintained at the reception to keep a chronological record of everyone from the outside who enters the office premises.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When a visitor wishes to see an official but the official is not available, which document should the receptionist use to record the visitor's brief message?
questions.explain: A **Caller's slip** (or telephone message pad) is designed precisely to jot down details of missed calls or absent guests so the intended recipient can be informed later.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The document usually maintained by a receptionist to keep records of contact numbers and addresses of important clients and organizations is the
questions.explain: A **telephone directory** is a reference document kept at the reception (or by switchboard operators) to easily find phone numbers and addresses for making outbound calls or answering queries.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A receptionist often handles letters delivered to the organization before passing them to the appropriate department. Which document is used to log these items?
questions.explain: To ensure letters and parcels are accounted for before internal distribution, the receptionist records them in the **incoming mail register**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Why is it strictly recommended for a receptionist to maintain an excellent appearance and dress neatly?
options: So they can leave the office early.
To intimidate visiting customers and salespeople.
Because their appearance reflects the corporate identity and first impression of the firm.
To ensure they are exempted from disciplinary actions.
questions.explain: The reception is the "face" of the business. A receptionist's neat dressing physically conveys professionalism, giving visitors a positive **first impression of the corporate identity**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of documents is mostly kept and maintained by a receptionist?
options: Balance sheet and profit and loss account
Articles of Association and shares certificate
Delivery note and store requisition form
Visitor's book and telephone message pad
questions.explain: The **Visitor's book and telephone message pad** (caller's slip) are core reception documents. Options A, B, and C belong to Accounting, Company Secretary, and Store departments respectively.
questions.subject: Business Studies
